heading: What the host does not do
body:
The host has no managed surface (a view that the host controls) for remote content. It has no always-on-top or opacity control beyond what the manifest grants. It has no global shortcut registry and no system tray API. These features were once a fixed list of verbs compiled into each host. A fixed list limits what an application can do. If an application needs one of these features, it uses the feature from its service. It uses it in the language of the platform it runs on.

The host also does not pass platform errors to the page. When a native service throws an error, the page gets only the fixed message "Native companion operation failed.", on every native host. The exception text stays in the app.
